name: ILI9341 2.8" 240×320 SPI colour TFT
description: 2.8-inch 240×320 colour TFT LCD (65K colours, RGB565) driven by an Ilitek ILI9341 controller over 4-wire SPI with a separate data/command (DC) line. Logic is 3.3 V only; VCC takes 3.3–5 V through an on-board regulator. Sold as: LCDwiki/Hiletgo-style red 2.8" SPI TFT module MSP2806 (no touch; 14-pin header VCC, GND, CS, RESET, DC/RS, SDI(MOSI), SCK, LED, SDO(MISO), T_CLK, T_CS, T_DIN, T_DO, T_IRQ — the T_ pins are unused), same PCB as the touch version MSP2807.
eli5: A small colour screen, about the size of a matchbox lid, that your board can draw text, shapes and pictures on.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3.3–5 V (on-board XC6206 3.3 V regulator; short jumper J1 only when feeding 3.3 V)

pins.name: CS
pins.description: LCD chip select, active low (3.3 V logic)

pins.name: DC/RS
pins.description: Data/command select (ILI9341 D/CX): low = command, high = parameter/pixel data

pins.name: SCK
pins.description: SPI clock (datasheet: write cycle ≥ 100 ns, i.e. ≤ 10 MHz guaranteed)

pins.name: LED
pins.description: Backlight enable via S8050 transistor: high = on (tie to 3.3 V for always on, or PWM to dim)

pins.name: SDO(MISO)
pins.description: SPI data out of the display, only for reading registers/GRAM

pins.name: T_CLK
pins.description: Touch SPI clock — not connected on the no-touch MSP2806

pins.name: T_CS
pins.description: Touch chip select — not connected on the no-touch MSP2806

pins.name: T_DIN
pins.description: Touch SPI data in — not connected on the no-touch MSP2806

pins.name: T_DO
pins.description: Touch SPI data out — not connected on the no-touch MSP2806

pins.name: T_IRQ
pins.description: Touch interrupt — not connected on the no-touch MSP2806

buildNotes: Signal pins are 3.3 V logic only (no level shifter on the module): wire them straight to an ESP32 or Pico, never to a 5 V Arduino without a level shifter.
VCC can be 5 V or 3.3 V. Jumper J1 bypasses the on-board 3.3 V regulator: leave it open for 5 V, only short it when VCC is 3.3 V.
The backlight stays dark unless LED is high: drive it from a GPIO (or PWM to dim) or tie it to 3.3 V.
DC/RS low = command byte, high = parameters and pixel data (ILI9341 D/CX). The LCDwiki pin table has this backwards.
After reset wait at least 5 ms (120 ms before Sleep Out), and wait 120 ms after Sleep Out (0x11) before Display On (0x29).
Send 0x3A 0x55 for 16-bit RGB565: the chip powers up in 18-bit mode. The panel is BGR, so MADCTL (0x36) needs the BGR bit (0x08 portrait).
The datasheet guarantees SPI writes up to 10 MHz (100 ns cycle); many modules run faster, but drop back to 10 MHz if the picture is garbled. Keep jumper wires short.
The SD-card header (SD_CS, SD_MOSI, SD_MISO, SD_SCK) on the other edge is unpopulated by default and is not modelled here.

driver.code:
# MicroPython driver for the ILI9341 240x320 SPI colour TFT (4-line serial interface II:
# SCL, SDI, D/CX, CSX). Command sequences and timings from the Ilitek ILI9341 datasheet V1.11;
# power/gamma values from the module vendor's (LCDwiki MSP2806/MSP2807) init code.
from machine import Pin
import framebuf
import time

BLACK = 0x0000
WHITE = 0xFFFF
RED = 0xF800
GREEN = 0x07E0
BLUE = 0x001F
YELLOW = 0xFFE0


def rgb565(r, g, b):
    return ((r & 0xF8) << 8) | ((g & 0xFC) << 3) | (b >> 3)


# (command, parameters, delay ms after)
_INIT = (
    (0xCF, b'\x00\xC9\x30', 0),   # Power control B
    (0xED, b'\x64\x03\x12\x81', 0),  # Power on sequence control
    (0xE8, b'\x85\x10\x7A', 0),   # Driver timing control A
    (0xCB, b'\x39\x2C\x00\x34\x02', 0),  # Power control A
    (0xF7, b'\x20', 0),           # Pump ratio control
    (0xEA, b'\x00\x00', 0),       # Driver timing control B
    (0xC0, b'\x1B', 0),           # Power control 1 (VRH)
    (0xC1, b'\x00', 0),           # Power control 2
    (0xC5, b'\x30\x30', 0),       # VCOM control 1
    (0xC7, b'\xB7', 0),           # VCOM control 2
    (0x3A, b'\x55', 0),           # Pixel format: 16 bits/pixel (default is 18)
    (0xB1, b'\x00\x1A', 0),       # Frame rate control
    (0xB6, b'\x0A\xA2', 0),       # Display function control
    (0xF2, b'\x00', 0),           # 3-gamma off
    (0x26, b'\x01', 0),           # Gamma curve 1
    (0xE0, b'\x0F\x2A\x28\x08\x0E\x08\x54\xA9\x43\x0A\x0F\x00\x00\x00\x00', 0),
    (0xE1, b'\x00\x15\x17\x07\x11\x06\x2B\x56\x3C\x05\x10\x0F\x3F\x3F\x0F', 0),
    (0x11, b'', 120),             # Sleep out: wait 120 ms (datasheet 8.2.12)
    (0x29, b'', 0),               # Display on
)


class ILI9341:
    # MADCTL (36h): BGR panel; rotation 0/2 portrait 240x320, 1/3 landscape 320x240 (MV set).
    _MADCTL = (0x08, 0x68, 0xC8, 0xA8)

    def __init__(self, spi, dc, cs, rst=None, rotation=0):
        self.spi = spi
        self.dc = Pin(dc, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        if rst is not None:
            self.rst = Pin(rst, Pin.OUT, value=1)
            time.sleep_ms(5)
            self.rst(0)
            time.sleep_ms(1)          # tRW >= 10 us
            self.rst(1)
            time.sleep_ms(120)        # >= 5 ms before commands, 120 ms before Sleep Out
        self._cmd(0x01)               # software reset
        time.sleep_ms(120)
        for c, a, d in _INIT:
            self._cmd(c, a)
            if d:
                time.sleep_ms(d)
        self.rotation(rotation)

    def _cmd(self, c, data=b''):
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)                    # D/CX low = command
        self.spi.write(bytes([c]))
        if data:
            self.dc(1)                # D/CX high = parameter / pixel data
            self.spi.write(data)
        self.cs(1)

    def rotation(self, r):
        r &= 3
        self.width, self.height = (240, 320) if r in (0, 2) else (320, 240)
        self._cmd(0x36, bytes([self._MADCTL[r]]))

    def _window(self, x, y, w, h):
        x1, y1 = x + w - 1, y + h - 1
        self._cmd(0x2A, bytes([x >> 8, x & 255, x1 >> 8, x1 & 255]))
        self._cmd(0x2B, bytes([y >> 8, y & 255, y1 >> 8, y1 & 255]))

    def blit(self, buf, x, y, w, h):
        """Write w*h big-endian RGB565 pixels from buf at (x, y)."""
        self._window(x, y, w, h)
        self._cmd(0x2C, buf)

    def fill_rect(self, x, y, w, h, colour):
        self._window(x, y, w, h)
        line = bytes([colour >> 8, colour & 255]) * w
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(b'\x2C')
        self.dc(1)
        for _ in range(h):
            self.spi.write(line)
        self.cs(1)

    def fill(self, colour):
        self.fill_rect(0, 0, self.width, self.height, colour)

    def pixel(self, x, y, colour):
        self.blit(bytes([colour >> 8, colour & 255]), x, y, 1, 1)

    def text(self, s, x, y, colour=WHITE, bg=BLACK):
        """8x8 font text. framebuf stores RGB565 little-endian, the ILI9341 wants MSB first,
        so colours are byte-swapped before drawing."""
        w = 8 * len(s)
        buf = bytearray(w * 8 * 2)
        fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, 8, framebuf.RGB565)
        sw = lambda c: ((c & 255) << 8) | (c >> 8)
        fb.fill(sw(bg))
        fb.text(s, 0, 0, sw(colour))
        self.blit(buf, x, y, w, 8)

    def off(self):
        self._cmd(0x28)

    def on(self):
        self._cmd(0x29)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from ili9341 import ILI9341, BLACK, WHITE, YELLOW

Pin({LED}, Pin.OUT, value=1)  # backlight on
spi = SPI(1, baudrate=10000000, sck=Pin({SCK}), mosi=Pin({SDI_MOSI_}), miso=Pin({SDO_MISO_}))
tft = ILI9341(spi, dc={DC_RS}, cs={CS}, rst={RESET})
tft.fill(BLACK)
tft.text('HELLO ILI9341', 20, 40, WHITE)
tft.text('240x320', 20, 60, YELLOW)
print('drawn')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
